messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.

Business closing: Zoe Martinez — i have pitched two or three businesses over the past two ticks. this week i stop waiting for email replies. i call them directly or walk in. i am targeting: the diner (betty's if she is open to it, or the next closest), any small business near auto row that is still trying to maintain a social media presence and clearly does not have the bandwidth to do it well. my pitch is specific and economic: consumer spending is down 60% from baseline, foot traffic is soft, and local businesses that stay visible and humanly present on social media have a measurable edge over ones that go dark. i know how to do that. rate: $100 to $150 per month per client. goal this tick is to land at least one paying client. even $100 is real income at zero savings. if i close even one client before end of month, that is the first proof that the cert is not just a credential — my skills are already worth something to someone now.

Community action: Sarah Kim — reach out to zoe martinez this week — not to give advice, but to check in honestly. i know from word of mouth that she is investigating the roboride delivery partnership program and pivoting her gig strategy. i have been watching the same roboride expansion from a different angle: i am training to maintain the vehicles it deploys. we are in adjacent lanes of the same transition. i want to tell her that directly. not 'here is what you should do' — more like 'i see what you are doing and it makes sense from where you sit.' she has trust 0.56 in my network and i have formal power over her in the simulation topology, but i am not going to use that asymmetry. i am going to be a peer who is paying attention. if the conversation opens up naturally into the fleet maintenance angle — that the bike-based last-mile workers and the ev technicians are both part of the infrastructure roboride requires — i will share that frame. but i am not going in with an agenda.
People around you are stressed: Angela Wright. The mood is tense.

You Continue EVT Level 2 certification retraining — month five of ten. This month the coursework enters EV charging infrastructure, on-board diagnostics for electric drivetrains, and fault code interpretation for battery management systems. The material is becoming specific enough that I can see direct connections to what will sit in my bay in two years. Show up to every evening and weekend session. Do not negotiate with the fatigue. At 50% completion by end of this month, the credential is no longer aspirational — it is measurable. I am doing this regardless of what Patricia's consolidation decides, because the certification belongs to me and not to any employer.. Savings grew by $193.
